notes:
{高野豆腐|こうやどうふ} is tofu that has been frozen and dried, giving it a unique spongy texture.

NAME ORIGIN:
- Named after {高野山|こうやさん} (Mount Koya)
- Buddhist temple complex in Wakayama
- Where this preservation method developed

ALTERNATIVE NAMES:
- {凍|し}み{豆腐|どうふ} (shimi-dofu) - Nagano region
- ⟦{凍|こお}り{豆腐|どうふ}→凍り豆腐：22852_kooridoufu⟧ (koori-dofu)
- Both mean "frozen tofu"

HOW IT'S MADE:
- Regular tofu is frozen
- Then slowly dried
- Creates sponge-like texture
- Absorbs flavor well when cooked

PREPARATION:
- Soak in water or ⟦{出汁|だし}→出汁：04917_dashi⟧ to rehydrate
- Squeeze out water gently
- Cook in simmered dishes

COMMON DISHES:
- ⟦{煮物|にもの}→煮物：04971_nimono⟧ (simmered in broth)
- {含|ふく}め{煮|に} (cooked in sweet soy broth)
- ⟦{精進料理|しょうじんりょうり}→精進料理：16101_shoujinryouri⟧ (Buddhist cuisine)
- {卵|たまご}とじ (with egg)

NUTRITION:
- High in protein
- Good calcium source
- Long shelf life
- Low calorie when rehydrated

BENEFITS:
- Shelf-stable (great for emergencies)
- Absorbs flavors well
- Vegetarian protein source
- Traditional Japanese food

RELATED FOODS:
- ⟦{豆腐|とうふ}→豆腐：04928_toufu⟧ (regular tofu)
- ⟦{湯葉|ゆば}→湯葉：07947_yuba⟧ (tofu skin)
- ⟦お{麩|ふ}→お麩：08112_ofu⟧ (wheat gluten)
- ⟦{厚揚|あつあ}げ→厚揚げ：07478_atsuage⟧ (fried tofu)

REGISTER: Neutral. Common in cooking contexts.
